items.title: A Ludicrous No-Brainer
items.author: Hinternet Editorial Board
items.quote: I, JSR, have been struggling these past few months to explain, in a first instance to myself, why it has lately felt so hard to write, or to write in a way that feels adequate to our moment, that feels true.
items.hook: Why is writing so hard in the digital age?

items.title: Remembering Francis Crick
items.author: David Eagleman
items.quote: He was one of the few people always willing to criticize his own ideas. He never filtered beliefs through his own ego and never hesitated to applaud other people’s theories.
items.hook: Discover the humility and intellectual rigor of Francis Crick.

items.title: The One-Way Speed of Light Problem
items.author: Dr. Manhattan
items.quote: Reichenbach proposes that we assign the time of the reflection or arrival event at B as: where ε is any real number from 0 to 1. When ε = 1/2, we recover Einstein’s standard synchronization convention; the reflection event is assigned the midpoint of the round-trip, and the one-way speed of light is c in both directions.
items.hook: Explore the hidden assumptions in measuring the speed of light.

items.title: Fake thinking and real thinking
items.author: Joe Carlsmith
items.quote: Map vs. world: Is my mind directed at an abstraction, or it is trying to see past its model to the world beyond?
items.hook: Explore the spectrum of 'fake vs. real' thinking

items.title: Sometimes the reason you can’t find people you resonate with is because you misread the ones you meet
items.author: Henrik Karlsson
items.quote: The third and deepest kinds of friendship, according to Aristotle, is a friendship of virtue. That is, you like a person because of their character. They might be fun, they might be useful, but even if they aren’t, you like them anyway.
items.hook: Discover the enduring power of friendships of virtue.

items.title: Face it: you're a crazy person
items.author: Adam Mastroianni
items.quote: When you fully unpack any job, you’ll discover something astounding: only a crazy person should do it.
items.hook: Discover why only a 'crazy person' should pursue certain careers.

items.title: The Decline of Deviance
items.author: Adam Mastroianni
items.quote: When you put all the data together, you see a stark shift in society that is on the one hand miraculous, fantastic, worthy of a ticker-tape parade. And a shift that is, on the other hand, dismal, depressing, and in need of immediate intervention.
items.hook: Discover why society's weirdness is disappearing

items.title: Ask Ethan: Why does something exist instead of nothing?
items.author: Starts With A Bang
items.quote: Perhaps the most remarkable fact about the Universe, if you think about it on a truly fundamental level, is that it exists at all.
items.hook: Why does the Universe exist instead of nothing?
